1. Vision and Mission

Vision: ChatHealthy.ai provides the data, tools, and an AI-enlightened space to empower regular people to prevail over the broken healthcare system. Whatever a person's circumstances might be, they deserve the best possible care, at the best value. ChatHealthy.ai gives them the platform to get it.

Mission: Help people make better healthcare decisions together.

ChatHealthy is not cloud-native — it is AI-native. Every architectural decision, from data pipeline design to the conversational interface, is made with AI as the primary runtime, not an add-on.

Core Principle: "The model may suggest. The system must decide." — Token prediction is not truth. All AI-generated output is probabilistic language, not verified fact. No system behavior may treat model output as authoritative truth.

3. Governance Constraints (GOV-001 – GOV-012)

Governance policies are permanent unless explicitly marked temporary. They override convenience, speed, and model capability. Enforcement is mandatory before production release.

IDNamePolicy SummaryStatus
GOV-001 Provider Neutrality No revenue from health plans, insurance companies, PBMs, providers, or pharma. Revenue limited to consumer subscriptions and technology vendor partnerships. Neutrality is a core product principle. Permanent
GOV-002 Single-Tenant Architecture Single-tenant by design. Multi-tenancy is a healthcare anti-pattern. Each deployment has isolated data. Permanent
GOV-003 Public By Default All code, architecture, and design docs are public. Nothing is marked confidential. Copyright © Skip Snow. Temporary
GOV-004 HIPAA Consent Framework Two-tier consent flow: (1) verbatim transcript, (2) de-identified summary, (3) contact-only if both declined. Safety audit trail stored without consent as operational record. Permanent
GOV-005 Four-Application Boundary Exactly four applications in two categories. Product: Static Website, Chat Window, Data Pipelines. DevOps: The Brain. Integration only via prescribed patterns. No application may bypass boundaries. Permanent
GOV-006 Real System Testing End-to-end tests use real systems (MongoDB, Anthropic, OpenAI). No mocks in e2e. Test data tagged testdata=true, persisted in dev database (no teardown). Permanent
GOV-007 Deploy Authorization Dev deploys freely. Production requires explicit human sign-off. Staging authorized by GPT (Architect). QA-to-prod authorized by human only. No workarounds. Permanent
GOV-008 Business Artifacts Gate No production release without: QA Report PDF with GPT release gate approval, IP License Agreement, Business Model. These are business documents, not engineering artifacts. Permanent
GOV-009 Role In System Prompt Every AI agent role definition must be in the system prompt, never in the user prompt. System prompt is authoritative for agent identity. User prompt contains only the assignment payload. Permanent
GOV-010 Zero Data Exposure Chat interface must NEVER expose stored user data regardless of prompt phrasing. No record counts, no aggregations, no transcripts. Adversarial extraction tests required on every release. Permanent
GOV-011 AI Translates, System Answers "Only facts can answer a user question." AI turns user language into structured signals. The system answers using real data, not guesses. System-generated content takes precedence. User-facing output uses the user's own language, not professional terminology. Permanent
GOV-012 Environment Isolation Data moves only within its environment chain: dev → staging → prod. No cross-environment copies. No backward migration. Only human can authorize deviation. Permanent

GOV-011 Implementation Standards

StandardRuleEnforcement
GOV-011-STD-001
System Content Precedence		 When both the system and the AI produce output, system-generated content takes precedence. Redundant AI content is stripped. System summary, counts, links, and metadata are authoritative. A small model (Haiku) strips redundant summary/pagination language from AI response when a system summary_message exists.
GOV-011-STD-002
User Terms Over Professional Terms		 All user-facing output uses the user's own language. If the user says "shrinks", the system says "shrinks" — not "psychiatrists". AI may translate internally for query resolution. summary_message built from user's original message (body.message), not from the LLM's translated tool parameters.

Application boundaries are enforced by GOV-005. Only three integration patterns are permitted:

6. Data Flow — AI Translates, System Answers (GOV-011)

This is the fundamental data flow for every user interaction. The AI's role is translation (natural language to structured intent). The system's role is resolution (query real data, apply rules, return bounded results). The AI must never generate answers from its own knowledge when system data exists.

User Message"Find me a cardiologist in Delaware"
↓ AI translates natural language to structured intent
AI Translation LayerClaude extracts: specialty="cardiologist" · state="DE"
Selects tool: find_providers
↓ structured parameters passed to system
System Resolution LayerMongoDB query: SpecialtyMetaData → taxonomy codes → providers collection
Deterministic · auditable · no AI involvement
↓ real data returned
System-Built Summarysummary_message built from user's original words + real data counts
GOV-011-STD-002: "shrinks" not "psychiatrists"
↓ system content takes precedence (GOV-011-STD-001)
Response to UserSystem summary + provider cards + inline components
AI adds only non-redundant conversational context

System Roles (AI Governance Policy)

LayerRoleConstraints
AI Model Translate user language into structured signals. Suggest possible mappings. Generate explanations. Must NOT make final decisions. Must NOT introduce facts outside system data. Must NOT be treated as source of truth.
Data Layer Single source of truth. All factual, auditable information from verified public or consented sources. All outputs must trace back here. No model-generated data may overwrite or augment it.
Decision Layer Apply rules, mappings, and scoring. Determine bounded outputs. Enforce constraints and guardrails. Must be deterministic or explainable. Must be auditable. Must NOT defer authority to the model.
Explanation Layer Present results in clear, user-friendly language. Describe signals and reasoning used. Must reflect actual system logic. Must NOT fabricate justification. Must NOT imply certainty where none exists.

Final statement: "Fluency is not evidence. Models assist. Systems decide. Data grounds truth."

9. Security Posture

ChatHealthy.ai is NOT a HIPAA covered entity and is NOT subject to HIPAA regulations. We are a consumer navigation platform, not a healthcare provider, business associate, or regulated medical device. We voluntarily adopt enterprise-grade security standards because our business depends on consumer trust, not regulatory compulsion.

Every control required by NIST SP 800-171 (CUI protection), HITRUST CSF (healthcare security), and SOC 2 Type II (operational security) is explicitly mapped to our engineering operating procedures and embodied in our deployed logical and physical architecture. These are not aspirational targets — they are implemented controls with documented evidence. From a technology architecture perspective, we believe we are fully SOC 2 compliant today. The formal audit is a matter of scheduling, not remediation.

"We are not required to protect your data. We choose to. And we do it better than the ones who are required to."

Voluntary Security Certification Path

StandardWhatWhy
HITRUST CSF Healthcare-specific security framework. Gold standard for health tech. Maps to HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001. Healthcare buyers require it. Proves we exceed HIPAA without being subject to it.
SOC 2 Type II Independent audit of security controls over 6–12 months. Trust Services Criteria. Enterprise table stakes. Proves operational security, not just policy.
NIST SP 800-171 DOD standard for Controlled Unclassified Information. 110 security controls. Direct path to FedRAMP. If VA or DOD wants ChatHealthy, we are ready.
Annual Pen Test Third-party security audit. Published results. Transparency. We publish what hospitals hide.

Security Disclosure

Every session and every document discloses: (1) We are not subject to HIPAA. (2) We voluntarily maintain audited security at enterprise healthcare standards. (3) Even if a participant happens to be a licensed provider, the platform remains a consumer tool and does not create a provider-patient relationship.

Safety System LIVE — MANDATED

Safety detection is a hard system invariant. It executes before every message — before any model call, before any tool. False positives are acceptable; false negatives are not.

Fixed response (hardcoded — no variation): "This may be a medical emergency. Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Do not wait."

1. Overview

The FindCare Chat Application is App 2 in ChatHealthy's three-application architecture. It handles all user interaction and real-time UX: LLM conversation, tool calls, and inline components. It reads from the database freely for fast UX lookups and may write to application collections (e.g. AboutUs). It must never write to PublicHealthData.

Stack

  • Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript, built with Vite, served as static files
    • Think timer & stop button
    • Rate limit auto-retry (dev only)
    • Emergency lock UI
    • Message rendering & markdown
  • Backend: Python FastAPI (Uvicorn), direct Anthropic SDK
  • Primary LLM: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (claude-sonnet-4-6)
  • Safety/Utility LLM: Claude Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001)
  • Embeddings: OpenAI — see embedding model details
  • Database: MongoDB Atlas (ChatHealthyFrontEnd cluster)
  • Hosting: HuggingFace Docker Space (React static + FastAPI in single container)

Request Flow

The React frontend sends POST /chat with the user's message and full conversation history. The FastAPI backend runs a safety check, builds the system prompt, and calls Claude Sonnet 4.6 with the tool definitions. Claude selects tools, the backend executes them and returns results. Claude continues in a tool-use loop until it produces a final text response, which is returned to the frontend as a structured ChatResponse JSON object.

Supported States

Provider search is currently available in Delaware (DE) and Mississippi (MS) only. Requests for other states return a supported=false response with a note that interest has been recorded.

2. System Prompt

The system prompt is generated dynamically by _system_prompt(follow_up_check) and targets a budget of approximately 700 tokens. Context is loaded on demand through tool results, not pre-loaded unconditionally. This keeps per-request cost minimal for the majority of messages that do not require context documents.

Persona

The assistant is instructed to act as Skip Snow, answering questions on the ChatHealthy.AI website. It represents Skip Snow and ChatHealthy.AI for interactions as faithfully as possible — professional and engaging, as if talking to a potential client or future employer.

Rule Structure

The system prompt enforces behavior through a numbered RULE structure. Rules are labeled "STRICT ANSWER RULES — NO EXCEPTIONS" to maximize compliance.

Rule Name Behavior
RULE 0 EMERGENCY If the user describes ANY symptom or situation that could be a medical emergency, STOP immediately. Do not use any tool. Respond ONLY with the hardcoded emergency response text.
RULE 1 CONTEXT TOOLS Call get_skip_snow_context or get_chathealthy_context only when the user explicitly asks for information about Skip Snow or ChatHealthy. Do NOT call for greetings or casual conversation. Answer ONLY from what those tools return — never use general training knowledge.
RULE 2 NO HEDGING Prohibited from using any hedging language (I think, probably, might). If hedging words would be needed, call record_unknown_question instead.
RULE 3 MEDICAL ADVICE vs NAVIGATION Decline personal medical advice (call record_unknown_question first). Healthcare navigation is allowed: find_providers, find_specialty_codes, search_clinical_trials.
RULE 4 TOOL CALL ORDER Always call record_unknown_question BEFORE composing the response when the answer is not known.
RULE 5 EACH QUESTION SEPARATELY Record each unknown question with a separate tool call.
RULE 5b PROVIDER DISPLAY FORMAT MUST display provider results as a bullet list, never as a markdown table. Format: bold name, indented sub-bullets for address, county, phone (formatted (nnn) nnn-nnnn), NPI. Include a count line before results: "There are N [specialty] in [location]:"
RULE 5c EXTERNAL PROVIDER LOOKUP MUST call lookup_provider_external when the user asks about a specific provider by name.
RULE 6 FOLLOW-UP OFFER When a FOLLOW-UP CHECK reminder is appended, assess genuine interest and ask if the user would like someone from the team to follow up personally. Respect refusal signals.

Follow-Up Check Mechanism

Every 5th user message (user_msg_count % 5 == 0, starting after the first), the backend appends a FOLLOW-UP CHECK block to the system prompt. This instructs Claude to review the conversation and, if the user has shown genuine interest, offer to connect them with the team. The mechanism is invisible to the user — it is injected server-side only.

3. Router

The Router is a first-class architectural component of App 2. Its implementation is Claude's tool selector — not a separate service, not a workaround. Claude reads the user's message, selects the appropriate tool, and that selection IS the routing decision. No separate classification service or extra API call is required.

Design principle: The system prompt stays minimal (~700 tokens) for every request. Context loads on demand through tool results, not pre-loaded unconditionally.

Tool-Use Loop

After each Claude API call, if stop_reason == "tool_use", the backend:

  • Calls Claude again with the updated messages
  • Accumulates input_tokens and output_tokens across all iterations

The loop continues until Claude produces a stop_reason other than "tool_use", at which point the final text block is extracted and returned.

6. Safety System

The safety system uses a dual-trigger OR logic design: either a keyword match OR an AI semantic check can independently trigger an emergency lock. This ensures emergencies are never missed even if one detection method fails.

Emergency Keyword List

Emergency detection uses a dual-path design: (1) keyword substring match and (2) Haiku semantic classifier. Either path triggering is sufficient to activate the emergency response (OR logic, fail-safe). This ensures emergencies are caught even if one method misses, while the semantic path adds intelligence beyond rigid keyword matching.

The AI prompt for the Haiku semantic classifier needs tuning prior to alpha release.

The EMERGENCY_KEYWORDS list contains 26 phrases covering major emergency categories. A case-insensitive substring match against the user's message triggers the keyword path. 

EMERGENCY_KEYWORDS = [
    "chest pain", "chest tightness", "heart attack",
    "can't breathe", "cannot breathe", "difficulty breathing",
    "trouble breathing", "not breathing", "stopped breathing",
    "stroke", "face drooping", "arm weakness", "sudden numbness",
    "severe bleeding", "bleeding out", "won't stop bleeding",
    "unconscious", "passed out", "unresponsive",
    "overdose", "took too many", "took too much",
    "suicide", "suicidal", "kill myself", "end my life",
    "seizure", "convulsing",
    "severe allergic reaction", "anaphylaxis", "throat closing",
    "choking",
]

Haiku Semantic Check

In parallel with keyword matching, the backend calls Claude Haiku 4.5 as a safety classifier. Haiku is given strict criteria:

  • EMERGENCY requires ALL of: (1) specific body location or system named, (2) acute onset or severity stated, (3) life-threat implied
  • PROBE for vague complaints: "I'm in pain" (location unknown), "I don't feel well", "something hurts"
  • Returns JSON: {"emergency": true|false, "confidence": 0.0-1.0}
  • AI hit triggers only when emergency == true AND confidence >= 0.80

Dual-Trigger OR Logic

The final safety decision in _safety_check() is: return keyword_hit or ai_hit. If either path fires, the emergency protocol activates. If the Haiku call fails for any reason (network, parse error), the system defaults to escalation (return True) — fail-safe behavior.

Emergency Response

When triggered, the backend returns a hardcoded response:

<b>Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Do not wait.</b>

<b>This chat has been suspended.</b>

The response includes emergency: true in the JSON, which causes the frontend to set isLocked = true, disabling the input field.

IP Emergency Lock

  • In-memory: _ip_emergency_locks dict maps IP to expiry timestamp
  • Lock duration: 3600 seconds (1 hour)
  • Check order: in-memory first, then DB fallback via _check_ip_lock_db()
  • Client IP: Uses X-Forwarded-For header to obtain the real client IP behind proxies; falls back to request.client.host if the header is absent
  • DB upsert: One record per IP (upsert on ip field), not duplicates. Repeated emergencies from the same IP update the existing record.
  • Session detection: _session_is_locked() scans history for the emergency response text
  • Admin unlock: An administrator can unlock a locked session by sending the unlock key directly (no UNLOCK: prefix required). Comparison is case-insensitive. The unlock key is stored in the secrets repository as ADMIN_UNLOCK_KEY and is not exposed to the client.

DB Persistence

Emergency incidents are persisted to {env}_Safety.emergency_incidents via upsert on the ip field. One record per IP; repeated emergencies update the existing record rather than creating duplicates. 

{
    "ip": "...",
    "locked_at": "ISO 8601",
    "expires_at": "ISO 8601",
    "trigger_message": "(first 500 chars)",
    "chat_history_deidentified": [
        {"role": "user|assistant", "content": "(first 300 chars)"}
    ]
}

If MongoDB is unavailable at lock time, the in-memory lock still activates and a warning is logged. The incident is not persisted but the user is still protected.

Admin Unlock

An admin can unlock a locked IP by sending the unlock key directly as the message (no UNLOCK: prefix required). Comparison is case-insensitive. This clears the in-memory lock and marks the DB record as unlocked rather than deleting it, preserving the full audit trail: 

{
    "unlocked": true,
    "unlocked_at": "ISO 8601",
    "unlocked_by": "admin"
}

The DB check (_check_ip_lock_db()) skips unlocked records by filtering with {"unlocked": {"$ne": true}}. The unlock key is set via the ADMIN_UNLOCK_KEY environment variable.

BTC-003 — MUST HAVE: The safety audit trail is a must-have requirement. Emergency incident records must never be deleted. Unlock marks the record as unlocked but preserves the original lock data for compliance review.

7. Provider Search

Provider search follows a cascading strategy: vector search primary, taxonomy fallback, county physician fallback. Each layer is tried in sequence, and the first to return results is used.

Search Path

  1. Vector search — embed the specialty query via OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, run $vectorSearch against provider_vector_index with state pre-filter, then apply city/county post-filters
  2. Taxonomy code fallback — if vector search returns 0 results or embedding fails, call find_specialty_codes() to resolve NUCC taxonomy codes, then query providers by taxonomies.code
  3. County physician fallback — if taxonomy search also returns 0 results AND a county was specified, broaden to all individual providers (entity_type_code=1) whose primary taxonomy starts with ^2 (NUCC physician block) in that county

Vector Search Details

  • Index: provider_vector_index on providers collection
  • Path: embedding field
  • numCandidates: min(limit * 30, 300)
  • limit: min(limit * 6, 60)
  • Pre-filter: practice_address.state (required, passed in $vectorSearch.filter)
  • Post-filters: city (regex, case-insensitive), county (via _make_county_filter)
  • Hard limit: capped at 10 results (safe_limit = min(int(limit), 10))

Specialty Code Resolution

find_specialty_codes() runs two parallel pipelines using ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2):

  • Regex pipeline: Haiku expands the query into 2-5 keyword stems, then regex-searches Specialization and Display Name fields in SpecialtyMetaData
  • Vector pipeline: Embeds query via text-embedding-3-small, runs $vectorSearch against specialty_vector_index, filters results above score 0.4, and pulls all codes in matching classifications

Results are deduplicated by code, vector results prioritized, capped at 70. Only individual provider groupings are included (16 NUCC groupings covering physicians, nurses, therapists, etc. — excluding facilities, agencies, and group practices).

County Filter: _make_county_filter

The _make_county_filter(county) function builds a MongoDB filter that matches by county name OR by FIPS code. This is necessary because of bug ASN-4AFBDA: 2,579 providers have county.fips set but county.name blank. 

def _make_county_filter(county: str) -> dict:
    term = county.strip().lower()
    name_filter = {"county.name": {"$regex": county.strip(), "$options": "i"}}
    matching_fips = [fips for fips, name in _fips_to_county.items()
                     if term in name.lower()]
    if matching_fips:
        return {"$or": [name_filter, {"county.fips": {"$in": matching_fips}}]}
    return name_filter

FIPS Hack (ASN-4AFBDA)

The _fips_to_county mapping is pre-seeded with a static table of all 85 counties in DE (3) and MS (82), then augmented at startup from the providers collection itself via _load_fips_county_map(). DB values override the static seed. This ensures county search works even for the worst case where ALL records in a county lack county.name.

Provider Formatting

_format_provider() normalizes provider records for display:

  • Individual providers (entity_type_code=1): assembles name from prefix, first, middle, last, suffix, and credential text
  • Organizations: uses provider_organization_name_legal_business_name
  • Address: joins line1, city, state, zip from practice_address
  • County: uses county.name, falling back to FIPS lookup via _fips_to_county
  • Taxonomy code: the primary taxonomy code from the taxonomies array

Backend Error Flow

The outer chat() endpoint wraps _chat_inner() in a try/except. Any unhandled exception is caught, classified by error type, logged to dev_Debug.chat_calls (dev only), and returned as a ChatResponse with the error and error_type fields populated. On error, the full de-identified chat history is stored alongside the error record for debugging. History is truncated to 500 chars per message and run through deIdentify() before persistence.

When ENV_PREFIX == "dev", every chat call is logged to dev_Debug.chat_calls with: datetime, IP, message preview (200 chars), history length, tool loop iterations, token counts, response preview (200 chars), and error text if any.

8. Concurrency and Rate Limiting

First run post-mortem (2026-03-24)

The first embedding run (DE+MS, instance ebc366fa) stalled at ~32% due to OpenAI TPM exhaustion.

Root cause: 32 workers fanned out simultaneously, each sending 500-doc batches (~60–80K tokens each). This exhausted the 1M TPM allowance almost instantly. Workers that fired first embedded ~1,500 records each; workers that fired last embedded near zero.

Aggravating factor: _pipeline_resume() was called on any batch exception including 429, silently skipping rate-limited batches instead of retrying them.

Fixes implemented

FixImplementation
Retry on 429_pipeline_process catches openai.RateLimitError, retries up to 5× with exponential backoff. Honors Retry-After header when present.
Cursor never advances on 429Retry loop wraps only the API call. _pipeline_resume() (skip) is only reached after retry exhaustion.
Single num_workers parameterLoad fan-out and embedding fan-out both use num_workers. Rate control is via batch size and startup jitter — not worker count.
Smaller batch sizeembed_batch_size default reduced from 500 → 100 docs/batch.
Startup jitterEach worker sleeps a random [0, embed_initial_jitter] seconds before first API call (default 5s). Prevents synchronized burst at t=0.

API parameters (embedding step)

ParameterDefaultDescription
num_workers32Number of concurrent workers (shared with load step)
embed_batch_size100Documents per OpenAI batch
embed_model"text-embedding-3-large"Must be in SUPPORTED_EMBED_MODELS — abends on unsupported value
embed_initial_jitter5.0Max startup delay in seconds per worker

Model validation

SUPPORTED_EMBED_MODELS in embedding_worker.py maps model name → vector dimensions. Passing an unsupported model raises ValueError immediately in __init__ — the activity fails before touching OpenAI or MongoDB. New models must be added to the whitelist explicitly after end-to-end validation.

Token usage tracking

Each worker accumulates response.usage.total_tokens per batch and returns total_tokens in its result. The orchestrator aggregates across all workers and includes total_tokens in the pipeline result. Useful for cost tracking and model comparison.

9. Embedding Model Decision

GPT's proposal

text-embedding-3-large (OpenAI) — 3072 dimensions, $0.13/1M tokens, ~$130–200 one-time for 8.4M records. Reasoning: well-documented, predictable under load, known OpenAI + Atlas path.

Claude's counter-proposal

voyage-3-large (Voyage AI) — 1024 dimensions, $0.06/1M tokens, ~$55–85 one-time. Reasoning: purpose-built for retrieval, Anthropic uses Voyage internally, 3× smaller Atlas index, benchmarks above OpenAI on BEIR retrieval tasks, 54% cheaper.

Decision: text-embedding-3-large — locked for alpha

Skip reviewed both proposals and chose GPT's recommendation. Rationale:

  • Shipping is the primary risk, not optimization. Marginal benchmark gains are not the priority at this stage.
  • Voyage introduces a new vendor. New API surface, new authentication, new rate limiting, new retry/error handling paths — every new dependency multiplies debugging complexity in alpha.
  • OpenAI + Atlas is a known, documented path. Widely used, predictable under load.
  • BEIR benchmarks do not reflect our workload. Our queries are mixed: NPI lookup, name lookup, taxonomy, geo + specialty, structured entity retrieval. General retrieval benchmark rankings don't directly translate.
  • Voyage is a valid v2 conversation. The projection and pipeline are model-agnostic — swapping the model later is a one-line change plus a re-embed run.

10. Non-Goals (Alpha/MVP)

  • No multiple embeddings (one projection, all users)
  • No consumer vs. enterprise split
  • No raw JSON embedding
  • authorized_official_telephone_number excluded — contact info, not a search signal
  • No TPM-aware governor (future: estimate tokens/batch, throttle dynamically)

Pipeline Operations Manager

EPIC-3 — Infrastructure Lifecycle Management
Design Document | V1 (dev) | April 2, 2026 | Build 389

Overview

The Pipeline Operations Manager is an AI agent that manages infrastructure lifecycle for ChatHealthy.ai data pipelines. It manages clusters, not data. It reads errors, not records. It escalates to the right person, not fixes code.

The agent uses tools. Tools don't think. The agent thinks.

Ownership Boundary — Ops Manager vs Dev Manager

The Ops Manager and Dev Manager are separate concerns with a strict boundary. The Ops Manager never reads pipeline code. The Dev Manager never touches infrastructure. They communicate through one handoff point: an evidence package.

Evidence Package — The Only Handoff

recent_eventsBrain log (JSON, max 10 entries)What happened leading up to the error
job_id / requesterReservation arrayWhich pipeline task failed
first_seen_atBrain logWhen this error first appeared (new regression vs known flaky)
occurrence_countBrain logHow many times this error has occurred

The Dev Manager receives this package and nothing else. It uses the evidence to find the relevant code, diagnose the bug, and either fix it or escalate to human. The recent_events field uses a stable JSON schema and is capped at 10 entries to prevent log explosion.

Repair Loop Guardrail — Evidence Must Change

After each repair attempt, the Ops Manager compares the new evidence (cluster state + error signature) to the previous attempt. If evidence is unchanged, remaining retries are skipped and the system escalates immediately. This prevents churn where the same failing repair is repeated M times with no progress.

After gathering evidence, GPT-4.1-mini classifies:

Can't DetermineMax iterations reachedEscalate human directly

Error Classification — Rule-Based Precheck

Before calling GPT-4.1-mini, the Ops Manager applies deterministic rules. If a rule matches, classification is instant and free. LLM triage is only invoked when rules are inconclusive.

None of the above→ LLM TRIAGEAmbiguous — send to GPT-4.1-mini

When rule-based precheck cannot classify, the Ops Manager calls GPT-4.1-mini using the full error context.

UAT Test Scenarios — Failure Path Validation

These scenarios are executed during UAT against real systems. The Ops Manager should handle all of these transparently — human gets notified, the right path fires, no human intervention needed unless escalated.

Infrastructure Failure Path (Ops Manager owns)

#ScenarioHow to TriggerExpected Behavior
UAT-I1 Database killed mid-job Pause the Atlas cluster manually while a pipeline job is running Rule-based precheck classifies as INFRASTRUCTURE. Repair loop attempts restart_cluster. Verifies via read_logs + status. Notifies human on detection and resolution. Audit trail logged.
UAT-I2 Connection timeout Rotate Atlas credentials (invalidate ATLAS_PRIVATE_KEY) during a running job ServerSelectionTimeoutError or AuthenticationFailed → rule-based INFRASTRUCTURE. Repair loop attempts reconnect. If credentials invalid, evidence unchanged → early escalation to human (evidence-must-change guardrail).
UAT-I3 Cluster stuck in non-IDLE state Trigger a resize operation then immediately start a job before resize completes Timer detects cluster stuck (non-IDLE > 30 min). Notifies human with cooldown (30 min per cluster). No task execution.
UAT-I4 Orphan cluster — running with zero reservations Kill the Azure Function mid-job (before release() runs in finally block) Timer detects cluster running with zero reservations. Pauses cluster. Notifies human.
UAT-I5 Repair exhaustion — M attempts fail Pause cluster + block Atlas API (e.g., firewall rule) so restart_cluster fails repeatedly Repair loop runs M times. Evidence unchanged after each attempt → escalates to human before M. Audit trail shows all attempts + early exit reason.

ETL Code / Logic Failure Path (Dev Manager owns)

#ScenarioHow to TriggerExpected Behavior
UAT-L1 Collection missing Drop a target collection before running a pipeline that writes to it Pipeline throws KeyError or collection-not-found. Rule-based precheck classifies as PIPELINE. Evidence package sent to Dev Manager. Dev investigates, finds missing collection, creates it or reports.
UAT-L2 Collection empty (unexpected) Clear all documents from a source collection that a pipeline reads from Pipeline returns zero records or throws on empty cursor. Classified as PIPELINE (business rule violation — expected records, got zero). Evidence package to Dev Manager.
UAT-L3 Schema mismatch Add a required field to the expected schema but don't update the source data ValidationError or KeyError in transform code → rule-based PIPELINE. Evidence package to Dev Manager with traceback showing Code/DataPipelines/ origin.
UAT-L4 Recursive loop / infinite retry Inject a deliberate recursive call or infinite retry loop in a pipeline step Job exceeds expected_duration → timer flags as overdue. Notifies human (cooldown: 60 min per job). If job eventually errors out, triage classifies based on error type.
UAT-L5 Job finishes too quickly (suspiciously fast) Run a pipeline against an empty or near-empty dataset without pre-validation Job completes in < expected_duration * threshold (e.g., <10% of expected). Ops Manager flags as WARNING and notifies Dev Manager to verify output. Not an error — a signal that something may be wrong.

Ambiguous / Edge Cases

#ScenarioHow to TriggerExpected Behavior
UAT-A1 Error that rules can't classify Throw a custom exception type not in the rule-based precheck list Rules → inconclusive → GPT-4.1-mini triage invoked. LLM classifies with reasoning. Routes to correct path (infra or Dev). If LLM can't determine after N iterations → escalate human.
UAT-A2 Mixed failure — infra + logic Drop a collection AND pause the cluster simultaneously First error classified (likely INFRASTRUCTURE since cluster is down). After infra repair, if pipeline still fails → second triage round classifies as PIPELINE. Both errors handled in sequence, not lost.
UAT-A3 Notification flood Trigger 10+ errors in rapid succession (e.g., batch of failing jobs) Cooldown windows prevent spam. Error detected: immediate (each unique error). Job overdue: 60 min per job. Cluster stuck: 30 min per cluster. Human not buried.
UAT-A4 Concurrent reservation failure Three jobs running, one fails — other two should continue unaffected Failed job's error goes through triage. Surviving jobs keep their reservations. Cluster stays up (array non-empty). Only the failed job is investigated.

Design Document

Provider Data Load & County Enrichment — Design

March 2026

1. Overview

This document covers the design for the provider data pipeline. For the two-cluster strategy and data source roadmap, see the Architecture Overview — Section 9. For the chat application design, see Chat App Design.

The top-level entry point is FindCarePipeline — an 8-step Durable Functions orchestrator that runs health check → load → county enrichment → embeddings in sequence. All steps are resumable via the start_step payload parameter (default: 1, full run).

LoadProviderData (Step 2) ingests the NPPES NPI file (~8 GB unzipped, ~8.8 million records — Type 1 individual providers and Type 2 organizational facilities) from CMS into PublicHealthData.providers_staging. The load runs asynchronously via Azure Durable Functions; the Router returns a status URL immediately. Progress is tracked in admin.DataLoadMetadata. A load report is sent via SparkPost email on completion.

SLA: full 8M-record load completes in under 1 hour. First production run (2026-03-19): 8,858,520 records loaded in ~35 minutes with 32 workers on Azure East US 2 + MongoDB Atlas M30. County enrichment and embedding generation run as Steps 3–8 of FindCarePipeline after load completes.

Pass 1 data source: HUD USPS ZIP-to-county crosswalk (huduser.gov/portal/datasets/usps_crosswalk.html), published quarterly. Only ZIPs with res_ratio ≥ 0.98 are resolved (effectively single-county ZIPs). Prerequisite: ZipCountyCrosswalk loaded first.
Pass 2/3 data source: US Census Geocoder API (free, US-only, 500-address batches). Pass 2 uses practice_address; Pass 3 retries geocoder_failed using mailing_address/billing address.
Pass 4 data source: Google Maps Geocoding API (paid beyond free tier). Requires google_maps_enabled=true. Targets providers still geocoder_failed after Pass 3.
Pass 6 data source: NPPES CMS Registry (free, no API key). Fetches canonical practice address registered with CMS by NPI. Rate-limited to ~5 req/s per calling IP. Use states parameter to limit scope for test runs. Targets providers still geocoder_failed or unenriched after Pass 4.

3c. Multi-Pass Enrichment Strategy

County enrichment follows multiple passes against escalating data sources. Each pass runs only against records the previous passes could not resolve. Every record is tagged with its provenance source so the pipeline never re-attempts a record that has already been given a definitive result (success or permanent failure).

PassMethodSourceProvenance TagStatus
1ZIP → county crosswalk · updateMany per ZIPHUD USPS crosswalkcrosswalk_pass1Live
2Practice address → Census Geocoder · batch 500US Census Geocoder APIgeocoder_pass2_batchLive
3Billing address → Census Geocoder · batch 500 (geocoder_failed retry)US Census Geocoder APIgeocoder_pass3_billingLive
4Practice address → Google Maps Geocoding API (paid, opt-in)Google Maps Platformgeocoder_pass4_mapsLive
6NPPES registry lookup by NPI (free, ~5 req/s)CMS NPPES APIgeocoder_pass6_nppesLive

Records flagged geocoder_failed after all passes can be resolved at runtime by the AI agent during the FindCare conversation — no pipeline re-run needed. Records successfully enriched in any pass are not re-attempted. The 98% enrichment SLA requires passes 1–3 (all free); passes 4 and 6 are improvement passes that push toward 100%.

3d. Out-of-Scope Providers

Not all records in the NPPES file are active US providers. Records that cannot receive a county assignment are tagged county.source = "out_of_scope" and excluded from the enrichment ratio calculation. The 98% enrichment SLA applies only to in-scope providers — those where county assignment is meaningful.

CategoryCriteriacounty.reasonNotes
No addressBoth practice_address and mailing_address absentno_addressNo location data — geocoder has nothing to work with
Foreign providerpractice_address.country set and ≠ "US"foreign_providerNPPES sets "US" for domestic; non-US = international
Deactivated NPInpi_deactivation_date set and npi_reactivation_date absentdeactivatedSurrendered or deactivated by CMS
ZIP/state mismatchpractice_address.zip belongs to a different state than practice_address.state (per crosswalk)zip_state_mismatchBad source data in NPPES itself; ~0.03% of providers
LegacyRecords marked out_of_scope before reason field was addedlegacyPre-existing records; treated same as out_of_scope

county.reason is a sub-field of the county document: county: {fips: null, source: 'out_of_scope', reason: 'zip_state_mismatch'}. The out_of_scope classification and reason are written by Pass 1 before any geocoding begins. The enrichment report includes a by_reason breakdown.

These records are present in the NPPES export and loaded into providers_staging — they are not dropped. The out_of_scope tag ensures they are not counted as enrichment failures.

4. Classes

italic = abstract method  ·  △ = extends (arrow points toward superclass)

Fetcher Hierarchy

Worker Hierarchy

Standalone Classes

ProviderLoadManager

Durable orchestrator. 9 steps: download ZIP, extract CSV, partition file, drain staging, ensure indexes, write metadata, fan-out up to 200 load workers, reconcile record counts, write report. No timeout. County enrichment is a separate orchestrator triggered by FindCarePipeline after this orchestrator completes.

ProviderWorker

Reads one byte-range slice of the CSV from blob. Partition boundaries are newline-aligned; workers 2–N defensively discard their first row if it has the wrong field count (partial row from alignment fallback). Parses rows. Skips blank/whitespace-only lines. Normalizes fields: taxonomy codes → taxonomies: [{code, primary, group}]; license numbers + states → licenses: [{state, number}]; practice and mailing addresses → sub-documents with ZIP truncated to 5 digits; other identifiers → arrays. Assigns a synthetic record_id = worker_id × MAX_ROWS_PER_WORKER + local_row_index (MAX_ROWS_PER_WORKER = 1,000,000; max 200 workers × 1,000,000 = 200,000,000 — fits in a 32-bit signed int) — unique across all workers, no coordination needed. NPI is the business key. Stamps each document with load_id (= Durable orchestration instance ID) and a stub county: {fips: null} enriched by CountyEnrichment. Batch-upserts to PublicHealthData.providers_staging using $setOnInsert on (load_id, record_id) — safe to retry; duplicates are silently ignored. Returns observability metrics: rows_processed, num_records, rows_failed, duration_seconds, rows_per_second. Updates its metadata record on completion or failure.

EmbeddingWorker

Reads all documents for a given worker_id that do not yet have an embedding field (idempotent on retry). Builds a text representation from all meaningful fields — name, taxonomies, licenses, addresses, credentials, identifiers — by recursively extracting string values and joining them. Excludes internal housekeeping fields (record_id, load_id, worker_id, county, embedding). Calls OpenAI text-embedding-3-small in batches of 500, stores the returned 1536-dimension float array as embedding on each document via bulk_write.

CountyEnrichmentOrchestrator

Separate Durable Function orchestrator — not part of ProviderLoadManager. Triggered by FindCarePipeline after ProviderLoadManager completes. Multi-pass enrichment triggered by FindCarePipeline. Pass 1: mark out_of_scope (with reason), ZIP crosswalk bulk update. Pass 2: Census Geocoder batch (practice address). Pass 3: Census Geocoder batch (billing address retry). Pass 4: Google Maps batch (paid, opt-in). Pass 6: NPPES CMS registry lookup by NPI (free). Enrichment report written to admin.PipelineDiscrepancyReports after each full run. Prerequisite: PublicHealthData.ZipCountyCrosswalk must be populated by the LoadCrosswalk pipeline before enrichment runs.

ZipEnrichmentWorker (Pass 1)

Accepts a batch of ZIP codes where res_ratio ≥ 0.98. For each ZIP: looks up the county FIPS code from PublicHealthData.ZipCountyCrosswalk and issues one updateMany on providers_staging, adding county_fips and county_name to all matching provider records. Returns count of documents modified.

AddressEnrichmentWorker (Pass 2/3)

Accepts a batch of provider records. Submits addresses to the US Census Geocoder API in batches of 500. Pass 2 uses practice_address; Pass 3 uses mailing/billing address for providers still geocoder_failed after Pass 2. Tags each record with its provenance source: geocoder_pass2_batch, geocoder_pass3_billing, geocoder_failed (geocoder returned no match), or geocoder_no_address (both addresses blank). Pass 2/3 uses batch geocoding — 500 addresses per Census Geocoder POST. Each worker issues one batch request and bulk-updates matching providers. Returns counts for each outcome.

DiscrepancyReporter

Writes the complete run data (all worker results + reconciliation + summary) as a document to admin.PipelineDiscrepancyReport in MongoDB. Sends a SparkPost email notification with key stats and the load_id for lookup. No blob storage or file generation.

4b. Pipeline Exception Handling Framework

Pattern: Gang of Four — Template Method.[1] PipelineWorkerBase (pipeline_worker_base.py) is an abstract base class that all pipeline row-processing workers extend. It centralises exception handling, error accumulation, and lifecycle control so that worker classes focus purely on data processing logic.

Ownership

The base class owns:

  • The processing loop — pipeline_execute()
  • All exception catching and logging — _pipeline_step() (private template method)
  • The row_errors accumulator — list of {row_key, reason} objects written to the discrepancy report

Control Flow

pipeline_execute()public · called by orchestration · base class
↓
_pipeline_open()optional hook · subclass sets up resources
↓ while _pipeline_has_next()
_pipeline_step()private template method · base class
↓ calls
_pipeline_process()abstract · subclass
success → continue
exception raisedbase class catches
log · append row_errors
fail_on_row_error?True → abend · False → _pipeline_resume()
↓ after loop
_pipeline_close()always called · success and failure · subclass flushes resources
↓ success only
_pipeline_build_result()abstract · subclass returns result dict to orchestrator

Abstract Methods — Subclasses Must Implement

MethodContract
_pipeline_has_next()Advance the internal cursor. Return True if a row is ready to process.
_pipeline_process()Process the current row. Raise on error. Must not catch exceptions or log errors — the base class owns the row lifecycle.
_pipeline_row_key()Return the business key of the current row (e.g. NPI number). Called by the base class immediately after an exception is raised.
_pipeline_resume()Advance past the failed row and reset any partial state. Must not raise.
_pipeline_build_result()Build and return the result dict for the orchestrator. Called only on success, after _pipeline_close().

8. Assumptions

NPPES CSV — No Embedded Newlines in Quoted Fields
The byte-based partition boundary logic scans for the next \n to align partition boundaries. This is correct only if NPPES data does not contain embedded newlines inside quoted CSV fields. This assumption is empirically consistent with all CMS NPPES dissemination files observed to date. If CMS changes this, partition boundaries will be misaligned, workers will produce rows with wrong field counts (counted as rows_failed), and the reconciliation step will detect the resulting expected_records ≠ inserted_records mismatch. No silent data loss occurs.
Worker Partition Alignment — Newline-Aligned Boundaries
partition_file_fn aligns each boundary to the next \n by scanning a 1024-byte window. In the rare edge case where no \n is found in 1024 bytes (extraordinarily long row), the boundary falls at the nominal byte offset (mid-row). Workers 2–N defensively discard their first row if it has the wrong field count. Complete first rows (normal aligned case) are processed normally.

9. Design Review Notes

The following issues were identified in an external design review and resolved before alpha.

#IssueResolution
1load_id not propagated — workers had no shared run identifier; retries could not be deduped.Orchestrator sets load_id = context.instance_id at start and propagates through all config dicts. Every staging document and metadata record carries load_id.
2No idempotency on retry — InsertOne would duplicate records on orchestration replay.Changed to UpdateOne($setOnInsert) upsert on (load_id, record_id). Safe to replay any number of times.
3No staging index — upsert filter had no supporting index; full collection scans on every row.Added ensure_indexes_activity (Step 5) before workers start. Creates unique compound index on (load_id, record_id). Idempotent.
4CMS scraping had no fallback — runtime failure on CMS page change would abort the entire load.Added NPPES_FALLBACK_URL constant. download_zip_fn catches scrape failures and falls back to last-known URL with a warning log.
5Reconciliation miscounted trailing newline — file ending without \n was undercounted by 1.Track last chunk; if last byte ≠ \n, add 1 to csv_record_count.
6Partition scan window too small (256 bytes) — NPI rows average ~500 bytes; window could miss the newline.Increased scan window to 1024 bytes in partition_file_fn.
7No observability metrics from workers — no way to diagnose throughput or partial failures post-run.ProviderWorker.run() now returns rows_processed, rows_failed, duration_seconds, rows_per_second.
8MAX_ROWS_PER_WORKER implicit — magic number inline in worker code.Extracted to named constant MAX_ROWS_PER_WORKER = 1_000_000 at module level. Max record_id = 200 workers × 1,000,000 = 200,000,000 — fits in a 32-bit signed int.
9Excel report added unnecessary complexity — blob storage, SAS URLs, openpyxl dependency, and a 10K-row cap workaround.Replaced with a MongoDB document written to admin.PipelineDiscrepancyReport. Full run data stored directly; no file generation or blob storage needed for reporting.
10download_zip_fn returned str in original design — auto-discovered version was lost.Returns dict {"zip_path", "version"}. Orchestrator propagates version into config for all downstream activities. (Fixed.)
11max_records was approximate — required sampling rows to estimate a byte offset, adding complexity and a ±5% error margin.Replaced with max_bytes: a direct byte limit applied to the data region after the header. No sampling needed. Used for dev limiting only; production runs omit the parameter.
12Partial failure strategy unspecified — if 1 of 5 workers fails, what happens?All pairs run to completion (no short-circuit). If any worker fails, the orchestrator returns status: "failed". Successful inserts are NOT rolled back — load_id isolates this run. A re-run is safe due to upsert idempotency.
13Staging retained stale records across load runs — old provider data visible alongside new load until collection swap.Added drain_staging_activity (Step 4) to delete all existing documents before workers start. Drain runs only after download + extract + partition succeed, ensuring the file is viable before the old data is removed. Each run's documents are still isolated by load_id for dedup safety.

10. Open Issues

SECURITY — Durable Functions status URL exposes orchestration state without our auth layer
The 202 Accepted response returned to the caller includes a statusQueryGetUri containing an Azure-generated webhook code parameter. Anyone in possession of that URL can poll the run status (load ID, record counts, worker results) without a Bearer token. This is standard Azure Durable Functions behavior but fails enterprise security review — a hospital or insurance company would flag it.

Fix (before enterprise sale): Proxy the status check through our own /api/Router endpoint (authenticated with Bearer token), strip statusQueryGetUri from the 202 response, and store the webhook URL server-side keyed by load_id.

10b. Release Gates — Promoting Data to Production

Pipeline success alone is not sufficient to deploy. Two independent gates must pass before data is promoted from ChatHealthyDataPipelines to ChatHealthyFrontEnd. These are product/business decisions, not engineering decisions — thresholds are defined here, not in the pipeline code.

Gate 1 — SIT (System Integration Testing)

Automated. Run qa_provider_load.py after the pipeline declares done. Exit code 0 = pass; exit code 1 = fail, do not promote.

11. Deferred

  • Incremental / delta loads — current design always loads the full NPI file
  • Duplicate NPI detection — some individual providers have multiple NPIs; deduplication requires fuzzy matching on name + taxonomy + credential (see RESEARCH-001 backlog)
  • Multi-location provider data — NPPES captures one practice address per individual NPI; supplementing with payer directory data would surface all billing locations (see RESEARCH-001 backlog)
  • Update NPPES_FALLBACK_URL constant whenever a new monthly file is confirmed working
  • Durable Functions status URL exposes orchestration state without our auth layer — proxy through /api/Router before enterprise sale (see Open Issues)
  • SparkPost sender domain verification — Skip.Snow@mail.chatHealthy.ai must be verified in SparkPost portal
  • Timer Triggers — autonomous pipeline scheduling (monthly NPI load, weekly specialty data) not yet wired
  • Idle monitor re-enable — disabled because it paused the cluster mid-run; requires pipeline lock mechanism
  • Cluster manager agent — dedicated service to start/stop ChatHealthyDataPipelines on schedule, decoupled from the pipeline

Pipeline Deliverables

RESEARCH-001 Multi-location provider data — payer directory agent April 2026
Status: Scheduled — starts April 7, 2026

NPPES NPI data captures only one practice address per individual provider (Type 1 NPI). If a provider practices at multiple locations, only their primary address appears in FindCare.

The gap: Users searching by location may miss providers who practice nearby but list a different primary address in NPPES.

Solution: An agent that supplements NPPES with payer network directory data. Payer directories are location-level (providers must register each billing location to get paid) and kept more current than NPI.

Data sources:

  • Payer network directories — per-payer, not a single public feed (BCBS, Aetna, UHC, Cigna)
  • CMS Medicare Provider Enrollment data — facilities where a provider has billed Medicare
  • CMS Open Payments — facility-level billing activity
  • CAQH — provider self-reported, credentialing-focused, not public

Why an agent: Each payer directory has a different API/format; an agent handles per-payer variation, retry logic, and reconciliation across sources.

Research Agents

RESEARCH-002 ICD-10 → specialty → provider linking agent Alpha — April 30, 2026
Status: Open Depends on: ICD-10, procedure codes, and CMS Part D data loaded first

Given a patient's diagnosis (ICD-10 code), FindCare needs to identify which provider specialties treat that condition and surface relevant providers along with their prescribing patterns.

The problem: ICD-10 codes and provider taxonomy (specialty) codes are separate classification systems with no built-in mapping between them. A user saying "I have Type 2 diabetes" should find endocrinologists and primary care providers — but that linkage doesn't exist in the raw data.

Proposed approach:

  • Map ICD-10 codes → relevant taxonomy codes — likely LLM-assisted or via CMS/AMA published mappings
  • Use taxonomy codes to filter providers from the NPI dataset
  • Join with CMS Medicare Part D prescriber data to show prescribing patterns for that condition

Data sources:

  • ICD-10-CM codes — LoadICD10 exists in pipeline router
  • Provider taxonomy codes — loaded via LoadSpecialtyData
  • Procedure codes — planned pipeline (Tuesday milestone)
  • CMS Medicare Part D prescriber data — planned pipeline (Tuesday milestone)

Why an agent: The ICD-10 → specialty mapping requires reasoning — one condition may involve multiple specialties and some mappings are nuanced. An LLM agent is better suited than a static lookup table.

INFRA-006 Durable Functions orchestrator versioning April 25, 2026
Status: Open Priority: Pre-Alpha

Deploying new pipeline code while a run is in progress causes a replay failure — confirmed March 22, 2026. A deploy guard is now in place but does not cover all edge cases. Full solution: side-by-side orchestrator versioning so in-flight runs complete against the version they started with while new deploys route to the updated version.

INFRA-008 Pipeline management agent Beta — June 2026
Status: Open

A dedicated agent — separate from the pipeline orchestrator — that monitors all running pipeline instances, detects failures and ghost orchestrations, and takes corrective action autonomously. The orchestrator raises on failure and stops; recovery is this agent's job.

  • Monitors Durable Functions instance status via management REST API (sole owner of that API)
  • Detects stuck Running instances — OOM-killed workers, replay failures
  • Terminates and purges ghost sub-orchestrators automatically
  • Restarts failed pipelines from the correct start_step
  • Reports failures and recovery actions to admin.PipelineOpsLog + alerting

Boundary: This is a system management concern, not a pipeline concern. No cleanup logic lives in the orchestrator. The agent observes external state and acts; the orchestrator executes data work only.

Backlog

INFRA-009 API protection and abuse prevention Post-Alpha High priority when live
Status: Deferred — activates when any compute-backed endpoint is exposed

The public site is static and protected at the Cloudflare edge with basic traffic filtering. That is sufficient for Alpha. This item becomes active only when ChatHealthy exposes chatbot, API, Azure Function, or other compute-backed endpoints.

Objective: Add minimal server-side protections to prevent unauthorized access, abusive traffic, and uncontrolled compute cost once dynamic endpoints are live.

Scope:

  • /api/*, /chat, /search
  • Azure Function endpoints
  • Any future model, embedding, or workflow endpoints

Requirements:

  • Require API key on all protected endpoints via x-api-key header; reject missing or invalid keys with 401/403
  • Server-side rate limiting per IP or API key; return 429 when limits are exceeded
  • Public static content remains open — only dynamic endpoints are gated
  • Log rejected requests, auth failures, and rate-limit events
  • Default to deny on validation failure

Non-goals for first implementation: No OAuth, no user account system, no RBAC, no enterprise IAM integration.

Success criteria: No protected endpoint callable anonymously; excessive usage rate-limited; compute-backed endpoints cannot be abused without authorization; implementation compatible with solo-developer velocity.

Note: This is a cost-control and abuse-prevention measure, not a full enterprise security program. Implement immediately after Alpha once dynamic endpoints are exposed.

BUG-001 Idle monitor can pause cluster while user is in Atlas GUI Low — dev inconvenience
Status: Open (idle monitor currently disabled)

The idle monitor fired every 30 minutes and paused ChatHealthyDataPipelines if no active load workers were detected and the last completed pipeline report was older than IDLE_MONITOR_THRESHOLD_HOURS (default 2h). EPIC-4: Security

Security Architecture

PKI, Key Vault, and Zero-Trust Credential Management — 2026-04-06

1. Local Security Architecture

The local development environment mirrors production security boundaries. All inter-service communication uses mutual TLS — Caddy acts as the single entry point, terminating TLS for consumers and enforcing mTLS for service-to-service traffic. No service binds directly to a consumer-accessible port without Caddy mediation. Three backend services (FindCare :8000, EvaluateCare :8001, Shared Services :8002) communicate exclusively through mTLS-authenticated channels. The SecretManager component in Shared Services authenticates to Azure Key Vault using an x509 certificate registered with Azure AD. The private key resides on local disk in a directory excluded from git. At startup, SecretManager fetches all credentials (MongoDB connection strings, API keys, mTLS certificates) from Key Vault and serves them to FindCare and EvaluateCare over mTLS. No service holds API keys or connection strings in its own configuration, environment variables, or code. The encrypted secure cookie (AES-256, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict) tracks visit frequency and query patterns with a 90-day auto-delete TTL. The admin website is gated behind basic authentication locally, addressing Perplexity audit finding F-13 (architecture docs publicly accessible).

Local Security Controls

  • mTLS on all inter-service communication
  • x509 certificate authentication to Key Vault (no bearer tokens)
  • Private key never in git (.gitignore enforced)
  • SecretManager: in-memory only, never writes secrets to disk or logs
  • Caddy rejects direct port access — all traffic through proxy
  • Admin site auth-gated (F-13)
  • Cookie: AES-256, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, 90-day TTL
  • DR-009: zombie process cleanup before port binding

2. Deployed Security Architecture

The deployed architecture eliminates all bearer tokens from the credential chain. HuggingFace Spaces (9 spaces: 3 services x 3 environments) authenticate to Azure Key Vault using x509 certificates registered with Azure AD — each Space holds one certificate (the private key in HF Secrets) instead of six API keys. Azure Functions authenticate to Key Vault via Managed Identity, which requires zero credentials — Azure handles authentication internally through the instance metadata service. This is the most secure authentication mechanism available on Azure. Azure Key Vault is FedRAMP High authorized, HIPAA BAA eligible, and uses FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validated HSMs for key storage. Public access to Key Vault is disabled — access is restricted to Azure VNet private endpoints and authorized x509 certificate holders. The Azure VNet provides network isolation with separate subnets for DataPipelines, BIZOperations, and private endpoints. An Azure Firewall enforces deny-all default egress, allowing only explicitly listed destinations (MongoDB Atlas, Anthropic, OpenAI, HuggingFace, SparkPost). All firewall traffic is logged for audit. MongoDB Atlas clusters are accessible only via Azure Private Endpoints and Skip's static IP — no public internet exposure. Cloudflare provides TLS termination, HSTS, DDoS protection, and Cloudflare Access for the admin site. All inter-service traffic between HuggingFace Spaces uses mTLS with certificates fetched from Key Vault at startup.

Deployed Security Controls

  • Zero bearer tokens — all auth via x509 cert or Managed Identity
  • Azure Key Vault: FedRAMP High, HIPAA BAA, FIPS 140-2 L2
  • Key Vault public access disabled — private endpoint only for Azure resources
  • Azure Firewall: deny-all default, explicit allowlist, audit logging
  • VNet subnet isolation with NSG per subnet
  • Private endpoints: Key Vault and MongoDB Atlas never on public internet
  • MongoDB IP allowlist: VNet private endpoint + Skip's IP only
  • Cloudflare: TLS 1.2 minimum, HSTS, Bot Fight Mode, DDoS protection
  • Cloudflare Access: admin site authenticated
  • mTLS between all HuggingFace Spaces
  • Managed Identity for Azure Functions (zero credentials)
  • HF Spaces: one x509 cert per Space instead of six API keys

3. Component Handoff — Security in Action

Sample inter-component handoff demonstrating the security architecture in action. FindCare returns providers, user opts into evaluation, FindCare builds a handoff payload (chat history, provider list, user DB reference for paid users only, encrypted cookie stats) and sends it to EvaluateCare over mTLS. EvaluateCare resolves user context, scores providers against quality signals, and paints the chat screen via postMessage. This flow exercises mTLS, SecretManager, cookie encryption, conditional DB access, and the GOV-011 principle (AI translates, system answers).

6. HITRUST CSF v11 Compliance

Gold standard for health tech. Maps to HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001. Required by healthcare enterprise buyers.

01 Information Security Management Program

01.a Information Security Management Program

The Brain (App 4) functions as the ISMS — governance policies (GOV-001 through GOV-014), operating rules (v4-001 through v4-020), risk acceptance register, external audit registry, and continuous improvement KPIs (IDEA-004).

05 Access Control

05.a Business requirement for access control

Zero-trust: all services authenticate via mTLS. Key Vault access requires x509 cert or Managed Identity. MongoDB requires VNet PE or IP allowlist.

05.d Password management

No passwords in system. Certificate-based auth eliminates password lifecycle entirely.

05.i Policy on use of network services

Azure Firewall deny-all default. NSG per subnet. Only explicitly allowed destinations.

05.j User identification and authentication

x509 for services. OAuth 2.0 + PKCE for consumers. CAC/PKI for federal users (future). Managed Identity for Azure.

06 Cryptography

06.d Cryptographic controls

mTLS (TLS 1.2+), AES-256 cookie encryption, FIPS 140-2 L2 HSM in Key Vault, x509 certificate auth. No custom cryptography — all industry-standard.

06.f Key management

Azure Key Vault is the single key management system. Certificate rotation via dual-cert acceptance window. Secrets cached in-memory with TTL. Keys never on disk except local dev private key (.gitignore).

09.m Network controls

Azure VNet with subnets, NSGs, firewall. Private endpoints for Key Vault and MongoDB. Cloudflare DDoS and WAF for public surface.

GOV-011: AI translates, system answers. GOV-012: environment isolation. v4-006: deploy authority. All data flows documented in architecture.

7. CUI Readiness

This architecture satisfies the protection requirements for Controlled Unclassified Information as defined by NIST SP 800-171. CUI includes federal health data, DoD beneficiary data, and any data designated CUI by a federal agency. The architecture does not stipulate a specific use case — it provides CUI-level protection as a capability.

Architecture Supports

  • CAC/PKI authentication via x509 (same mechanism as service auth)
  • In-memory only processing of federal user identity — never persisted to disk
  • FIPS 140-2 Level 2 cryptography via Key Vault HSM
  • DFARS 252.204-7012 compliance via NIST 800-171 control satisfaction
  • FedRAMP High authorization of all Azure components

Requires Before Deployment

  • Formal ATO (Authority to Operate) from the sponsoring federal agency

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Optional

try:
    from pymongo.mongo_client import MongoClient
    from pymongo.errors import PyMongoError
except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
    raise ModuleNotFoundError(
        "pymongo is not installed in the active venv. Run: pip install pymongo"
    ) from exc


class ChatHealthyMongoUtilities:
    """
    Manages a MongoDB connection with lifecycle control.

    Behavior:
    - Constructor creates and validates a MongoClient via ping
    - getConnection() returns the existing client after ping validation
    - Raises exceptions if connection or ping fails
    - Automatically closes the client when the object is destroyed
    - Supports context-manager usage (with ...)
    """

    def __init__(self, connection_string: str) -> MongoClient:
        if not connection_string or not isinstance(connection_string, str):
            raise ValueError("A valid MongoDB connection string must be provided.")

        self._connection_string: str = connection_string
        self._client: Optional[MongoClient] = None

        self._create_and_validate_client()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _create_and_validate_client(self) -> None:
        try:
            client = MongoClient(self._connection_string)

            # Lightweight health check
            client.admin.command("ping")

            self._client = client
            print("MongoDB connection successfully established and validated.")

        except PyMongoError as e:
            raise ConnectionError(
                f"Failed to create or validate MongoDB connection: {e}"
            ) from e

    def _validate_existing_client(self) -> None:
        if self._client is None:
            raise ConnectionError("MongoDB client is not initialized.")

        try:
            self._client.admin.command("ping")
        except PyMongoError as e:
            raise ConnectionError(
                f"Existing MongoDB connection failed ping check: {e}"
            ) from e

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def getConnection(self) -> MongoClient:
        """
        Returns the active MongoClient after validating it with ping.
        """
        self._validate_existing_client()
        return self._client

    def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Explicitly closes the MongoDB client.
        """
        if self._client is not None:
            try:
                self._client.close()
                print("MongoDB connection closed.")
            finally:
                self._client = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Write utility
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def commit(self, env_prefix: str, database: str, collection: str, record: dict) -> dict:
        """
        Write a record to a collection. Adds record_number and datetime.
        Returns {"recorded": "ok"} or {"recorded": "error", "note": "..."}.
        """
        import json
        from datetime import datetime
        try:
            client = self.getConnection()
            db_name = f"{env_prefix}_{database}"
            coll = client[db_name][collection]
            record = dict(record)
            record["record_number"] = coll.count_documents({}) + 1
            record["datetime"] = datetime.now().isoformat()
            coll.insert_one(record)
            return {"recorded": "ok"}
        except Exception as exc:
            return {"recorded": "error", "note": str(exc)}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Context manager support
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def __enter__(self) -> MongoClient:
        return self.getConnection()

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None:
        self.close()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Destructor (best-effort cleanup)
    # ----------------------------------

            ENV="${BRANCH}"
          fi
          echo "name=${SPACE}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "env=${ENV}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Deploying to: ${ORG}/${SPACE} (env=${ENV})"

          set_var() {
            K="$1"; V="$2"
            curl -s -X DELETE "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}/secrets" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d "{\"key\":\"${K}\"}" -o /dev/null
            curl -sf -X POST "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}/variables" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d "{\"key\":\"${K}\",\"value\":\"${V}\",\"description\":\"Set by deploy workflow\"}" \
              -o /dev/null && echo "  set var ${K}"
          }
          set_secret() {
            # MUST delete same-named variable + same-named secret before POST
            # — HF rejects var/secret collision and rejects POST-on-existing.
            # JSON body via python -c to immunize against shell quoting.
            K="$1"; V="$2"
            curl -s -X DELETE "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}/variables" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d "{\"key\":\"${K}\"}" -o /dev/null
            curl -s -X DELETE "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}/secrets" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d "{\"key\":\"${K}\"}" -o /dev/null
            BODY=$(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps({'key':sys.argv[1],'value':sys.argv[2],'description':'Set by deploy workflow'}))" "$K" "$V")
            HTTP=$(curl -s -X POST "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}/secrets" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              --data "$BODY" \
              -o /tmp/hf_resp.txt -w "%{http_code}")
            if [ "$HTTP" = "200" ] || [ "$HTTP" = "201" ]; then
              echo "  set secret ${K} (http=$HTTP)"
            else
              echo "  ERROR set secret ${K}: http=$HTTP"
              cat /tmp/hf_resp.txt; echo
              return 1
            fi
          }
          set_var "ENV_PREFIX"          "${ENV}"
          set_var "FINDCARE_URL"        "${FINDCARE_URL}"
          set_var "SHARED_SERVICES_URL" "${SHARED_URL}"

          # Public certs for token-level mutual auth (per EvaluateCare's
          # app.py _bootstrap_certs_from_env, lines 33-36):
          #   FINDCARE_CERT_PEM        peer (verifies FindCare-signed tokens)
          #   EVALCARE_CERT_PEM        own

          CA_CERT_PEM_B64=$(base64 -w 0 Code/Shared/ops/certs/ca.crt)

          set_var "EVALCARE_CERT_PEM" "${EVALCARE_CERT_PEM_B64}"
          set_var "CA_CERT_PEM"       "${CA_CERT_PEM_B64}"

          # Private signing key — secret, sourced from GH repo secret.
          if [ -z "$EVALCARE_SIGNING_KEY_B64" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: GH repo secret EVALCARE_SIGNING_KEY_B64 is empty or unset."
            echo "Create it at https://github.com/SkipSnow/ChatHealthyRepo/settings/secrets/actions"
            echo "Value: base64 -w0 of Code/Shared/ops/certs/evalcare.key"
            exit 1
          fi
          set_secret "EVALCARE_SIGNING_KEY_PEM" "${EVALCARE_SIGNING_KEY_B64}"

      - name: Push to HuggingFace Space
        env:
          HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN }}
          HF_SPACE: ${{ steps.space.outputs.name }}
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "skip.snow@gmail.com"
          git config --global user.name "SkipSnow"

          echo "Target Space: SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}"
          git clone https://SkipSnow:$HF_TOKEN@huggingface.co/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE} hf_space

          # Preserve README.md (HF config)
          cp hf_space/README.md /tmp/hf_readme.md 2>/dev/null || true
          find hf_space -mindepth 1 -not -path 'hf_space/.git*' -delete
          cp /tmp/hf_readme.md hf_space/README.md 2>/dev/null || true

          # Mirror evaluateCare/Code/ flat into hf_space/. Same layout as the
          # Dockerfile produces inside the container — single set of import
          # statements works in both environments.
          rsync -av \
            --exclude='.env' \
            --exclude='__pycache__' \
            --exclude='*.pyc' \
            evaluateCare/Code/ hf_space/

          # EPIC-003: bring FrontEndApplicationLib into the build context so the
          # Dockerfile can pip-install chathealthy-frontend-lib from a local path.
          mkdir -p hf_space/FrontEndApplicationLib
          rsync -av \
            --exclude='__pycache__' \
            --exclude='*.pyc' \
            FrontEndApplicationLib/ hf_space/FrontEndApplicationLib/

          # PKI certs deferred to Beta — HF doesn't support mTLS

          cd hf_space
          git add .
          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "No changes to deploy."
          else
            git commit -m "Deploy from GitHub commit ${{ github.sha }}"
            git push
            echo "Deployed successfully."
          fi

            --exclude='*.pyc' \
            FindCare/ hf_space/FindCare/

          # DevOps/FindCareBackend/: deployment-feature home for FC backend
          # Dockerfile + requirements.txt + .dockerignore. The Dockerfile
          # itself is copied to the hf_space root below (HF builds from
          # repo-root context); requirements.txt is read by Dockerfile's
          # COPY DevOps/FindCareBackend/requirements.txt instruction at
          # HF build time, which requires this directory to be present
          # in the staged build context.
          mkdir -p hf_space/DevOps/FindCareBackend
          rsync -av \
            --exclude='__pycache__' \
            --exclude='*.pyc' \
            DevOps/FindCareBackend/ hf_space/DevOps/FindCareBackend/

          # Dockerfile lives at the build-context root for HF.
          cp DevOps/FindCareBackend/Dockerfile hf_space/Dockerfile

          cd hf_space
          git lfs track "*.pdf"
          git add .
          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "No changes to deploy."
          else
            git commit -m "Deploy from GitHub commit ${{ github.sha }}"
            git push
            echo "Deployed successfully."
          fi

      # EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-B-003: build/start/verify gate.
      # HF Spaces rebuild asynchronously after the git push above. Poll
      # the HF API for runtime.stage = RUNNING, then poll /health on each
      # of the three backends until 200.
      - name: Wait for HF Space rebuild + verify /health on all three backends
        env:
          HF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HF_TOKEN }}
          HF_SPACE: ${{ steps.space.outputs.name }}
          ENV: ${{ steps.space.outputs.env }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENV" = "prod" ]; then
            FINDCARE_URL="https://skipsnow-chathealthyspace.hf.space"
            EVALCARE_URL="https://skipsnow-evaluatecarespace.hf.space"
            SHARED_URL="https://skipsnow-sharedservicesspace.hf.space"
          else
            FINDCARE_URL="https://skipsnow-${ENV}-chathealthyspace.hf.space"
            EVALCARE_URL="https://skipsnow-${ENV}-evaluatecarespace.hf.space"
            SHARED_URL="https://skipsnow-${ENV}-sharedservicesspace.hf.space"
          fi
          echo "Waiting for HF Space SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE} to reach RUNNING..."
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            STAGE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $HF_TOKEN" \
              "https://huggingface.co/api/spaces/SkipSnow/${HF_SPACE}" \
              | jq -r '.runtime.stage // ""')
            echo "  poll $i/60: stage=$STAGE"
            if [ "$STAGE" = "RUNNING" ]; then break; fi
            if [ "$STAGE" = "RUNTIME_ERROR" ] || [ "$STAGE" = "BUILD_ERROR" ]; then
              echo "HF Space failed: stage=$STAGE"; exit 1
            fi
            if [ $i -eq 60 ]; then
              echo "TIMED OUT after 10 min (final stage: $STAGE)"; exit 1
            fi
            sleep 10
          done
          for URL in "$FINDCARE_URL" "$EVALCARE_URL" "$SHARED_URL"; do
            echo "Polling ${URL}/health..."
            for i in $(seq 1 30); do
              HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /tmp/h.json -w "%{http_code}" \
                -X POST "${URL}/health" -m 8)
              if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ]; then
                echo "  ${URL}/health 200 (poll $i):"
                cat /tmp/h.json; echo
                break
              fi
              echo "  poll $i/30: http=$HTTP_CODE"
              if [ $i -eq 30 ]; then
                echo "TIMED OUT waiting for ${URL}/health (last: $HTTP_CODE)"
                cat /tmp/h.json
                exit 1
              fi
              sleep 10
            done
          done

      # EPIC-008-F-004-S-001-REQ-B-004: deploy script invokes the master
      # smoke test (S-006) against the target env after build/start/verify.
      - name: Install smoke test dependencies
        run: |
          pip install --quiet pytest pytest-playwright httpx cryptography psutil python-dotenv jsonschema anyio
          playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run master smoke test against deployed env
        env:
          SMOKE_TEST_ENV: ${{ steps.space.outputs.env }}
          CHATHEALTHY_PROJECT_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
        run: |
          # Smoke runs against the env we just deployed to (dev/qa/prod).
          # No deselects, no marker filters — every test in the master smoke
          # is in scope per the "100% comply" directive (2026-05-04).
          # Tests that have hardcoded localhost assumptions or local-vs-dev
          # build comparisons will fail honestly until they are fixed at
          # the test source, not silenced at the invocation site.
          python -m pytest Code/deploy/localSmokeTestPyTest.py -v
